fixes.result: Recheck original idle/absolute deadlines after UPDATE and before COMMIT; rollback credential generation and tombstone on expiry or clock failure, preserving the caller savepoint. Timely mutation remains valid if only COMMIT acknowledgement is delayed.
Reset successful-proof failure budgets with UPDATE, preserving the mutex row across a competing no-op INSERT / lock UPDATE acquisition.
fixes.classification: Availability / synchronization lifecycle; no authentication bypass demonstrated.
fixes.storage_impact: One budget/mutex row remains per used subject+purpose pair, including successful proofs. No TTL pruning; challenge cleanup does not delete mutex rows. SQL locks end with the transaction.

independent_review.scope: Independent read-only review of the final rotation expiry guard and OTP budget mutex retention change; production source was not edited by this reviewer.

rotation.changed_behavior: After successful conditional UPDATE and before transaction commit, re-evaluate the selected original row against a fresh clock; reject with the existing InvalidArgumentException when idle or absolute expiry has been reached.
rotation.atomicity: Existing transaction wrapper rolls back both new generation and old credential tombstone on guard rejection or a clock exception. Nested savepoint rejection preserves unrelated work in the caller transaction.
rotation.negative_control: A timely UPDATE followed by late commit acknowledgement remains accepted. Checking the original expiry after commit would reject an already timely rotation; retain the three reason-specific controls.
rotation.concurrent_touch: A touch committed after the initial SELECT can make the selected original deadline stale, so the guard can reject conservatively. The initial check already has this snapshot limitation; the contract does not guarantee rotation success across all simultaneous touches. No authentication extension is granted by this rejection.
rotation.locking_decision: Do not introduce FOR UPDATE or another SELECT for this confirmed expiry defect. Added locking would change contention/order semantics. In particular do not lock rowByUuid globally: it also serves isGrantCurrent and find.
rotation.phpstan_contract: The final @phpstan-impure annotation on now() accurately expresses advancing clock observations. It changes no PHP runtime behavior and avoids relying on repeated-call result caching in static analysis.

otp.changed_behavior: On successful challenge claim, reset failures to zero and window_started_at to the refreshed verification time by UPDATE while preserving the subject/purpose mutex row and lock_version.
otp.failure_path_addressed: Deleting the row after another operation has passed its INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING but before its mutex UPDATE can make that UPDATE affect zero rows and throw Could not acquire OTP budget lock. Retaining the row removes that deletion boundary for both issuance and verification.
otp.window_semantics: Success resets counters and starts a fresh fixed budget window at successful verification time. Old deletion recreated the window on a later acquire; retaining and explicitly resetting the window provides the promised successful-proof budget reset without erasing the mutex. Issuance already creates the initial window, so the contract does not promise anchoring every window to the first failed attempt.
otp.retention: At most one live row per distinct used subject_uuid/purpose pair under the composite primary key. This is a cardinality bound per pair, not a global storage bound or TTL purge. Challenge cleanup does not delete budget rows, as README now states. The retained row holds counters and coordination state, not OTP codes; the SQL row lock ends at transaction end.
otp.cleanup_recommendation: Do not add general expiry deletion of mutex rows as part of this patch: deleting rows while acquisitions are in flight would reintroduce the race. Any future subject-lifecycle purge needs explicit coordination.
otp.test_review: The tests exercise observable successful proof, budget reset, both pending-operation cases, and one-time consumption. Logger callback deterministically models an interleaving and asserts that the boundary was reached; it does not emulate native separate-connection contention.

postgresql_static_corroboration.kind: Source-based corroboration, not native concurrency verification
postgresql_static_corroboration.observation: The existing-conflict DO NOTHING branch performs the visibility check then returns, unlike the DO UPDATE tuple-update path; this supports the interleaving without claiming every database/isolation level has identical behavior.

independent_review.verification_provenance: This reviewer inspected source, final test artifacts, XML counts and logs; no broad or focused PHP suite was re-executed by this reviewer. Runtime executions belong to the parent/other agent and are independently read here.
remaining_limits: No native cross-connection PostgreSQL concurrency run or lock certification. SQLite Cycle compilation strips FOR UPDATE and cannot establish native row-lock ordering.
Concurrent touch may cause conservative rotation rejection under a stale selected row, as described above.
OTP budget rows have per-pair cardinality retention and no automatic TTL cleanup.

finding.description: Successful verification deleted the subject/purpose mutex row after a competing issue/verify had completed its no-op INSERT, making the next lock UPDATE affect zero rows and throw.
finding.fix: Keep the mutex row and reset failures/window_started_at via UPDATE.
finding.evidence_boundary: Deterministic public Cycle driver logger schedules a second valid public verify between the first operation no-op INSERT and lock UPDATE, using SQLite to verify resulting state. PostgreSQL Read Committed schedule is supported by primary docs/source; native contention is not certified.
finding.storage_impact: One non-secret budget/mutex row persists per issued subject/purpose even after successful proof. Existing cleanup only prunes challenge history. Locks still release at transaction commit; counters reset on success; existing BIGINT lock_version schemas suffice.

red.control: Sequential valid proof resets aggregate failures; passes before fix.

method_consistency_review.other_scope: No additional confirmed defect from targeted stale-credential, subject/browser-binding, compensation and request-state review. RememberMe stale AuthSession candidate rejected because AuthenticationMiddleware removes prior concrete state; WebAuthn zero-counter updates intentionally allow distinct ceremonies and deletion remains CAS-protected.

recheck2.evidence_boundary: Controlled public Cycle driver boundaries and SQLite verify expiry/rollback/state outcomes. PostgreSQL Read Committed semantics support the OTP schedule; no native independent-connection concurrency certification is claimed.
false_positive_filters: Do not invalidate a timely rotation solely because acknowledgement of COMMIT occurs after the original deadline.
A stale snapshot can conservatively reject rotation when activity changes concurrently. FOR UPDATE changes locking semantics and is not required for this expiry correction.
AuthenticationMiddleware removes the prior concrete authentication-state type before replacement; a fabricated stale attribute outside that pipeline does not prove a RememberMe defect.
Distinct single-use WebAuthn ceremonies with zero sign counters do not themselves require a global revision rejection.
Deferred credential delivery is not an atomic distributed transaction with subsequent revocation or arbitrary network I/O.

fixes.classification: persisted-state model integrity and consistent parameter validation
fixes.result: A private hydrateCredential helper reuses the existing TotpCredential constructor for active and pending state before cryptographic verification and conditional writes; find uses the same helper. No new public API or new allowed-value policy.
fixes.trust_boundary: Requires malformed/imported stored metadata. The public enrollment HTTP flow writes 30-second SHA-1 defaults. This is not evidence of a remote authentication bypass.
fixes.invariants: Invalid active metadata does not claim last_used_step. Invalid pending metadata leaves active and pending columns unchanged, and the previous valid factor remains usable. The existing exception behavior of the model is preserved.
fixes.controls: Valid periods 15 and 120, SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512, upper/mixed-case digest names and 6/7/8 digits remain supported. No schema or Composer changes.
fixes.parameter_policy_note: The 15–120-second, 6–8-digit and SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512 restrictions are existing Componenta TotpCredential model rules, not universal limits imposed by the TOTP RFC.

write_failure_probes.status: Passed once after the parent declared integration and integration84 stable with Symfony 8.1.13 patches.
write_failure_probes.method: Seven scenarios inject real SQLite write exceptions through triggers; one injects an identity lookup exception. The WebAuthn scenario starts with a real ECDSA signed assertion.
results: Recovery-code regeneration rolls back the old-batch deletion and first new insert when the next insert fails; previous codes remain single-use and wrong-subject consumption is denied.
TOTP pending replacement, activation and replay-counter write failures preserve storage; previous factor and pending enrollment remain usable after removing the injected fault.
RememberMe rotation and session-binding write failures preserve the retryable grant; binding retry remains idempotent.
WebAuthn failed credential update propagates after ceremony consumption; the ceremony is not resurrected, the counter remains unchanged and a new valid signed ceremony succeeds.
MagicLink identity lookup failure propagates after consumption; the proof remains consumed, replay avoids another identity read, and a fresh valid link succeeds.
Password persistence/reset atomicity is explicitly owned by the application reset service; no unsupported distributed-transaction guarantee was introduced.
No additional confirmed defect in the other five scoped packages. Prior expiry and OTP mutex work was not expanded.

root_contract_review.conclusion: No additional confirmed defect in these scoped source contracts in this pass.
checks: Session and pre-authentication security reads use the writer, not a lagging read connection.
Session housekeeper repeats expiry/revocation predicates before deletion; credential token cleanup selects immutable hashes.
Subject mutex rows in session create/revokeAll are retained; no OTP-style successful-operation deletion exists there.
Session rotation compensation and expiry guard retain the transaction/savepoint boundary checked in the previous pass.
Soft-failed HTTP candidates roll back only their registrations; ownership controls deferred-publication cancellation.
Authentication state removal includes the previous concrete state type; same-subject state preservation is deliberate.
Credential value objects/transport reject malformed bearer or cookie input before authentication.
false_positive_filters: Public session registry listings are snapshots and never authenticate a bearer; no universal post-I/O freshness guarantee was invented.
Caller-built AuthSession/Grant objects are trusted service inputs; fabricated inconsistent objects do not establish a remote authentication path.
A token whose creation consumed its TTL is rejected by subsequent proof validation; issuance does not itself authenticate it.
No distributed atomicity is promised between a successful DB read, later revocation and arbitrary external I/O.

reasoning: Private hydrateCredential is now the single conversion path for active reads, active verification and pending activation. It constructs the existing TotpCredential value with the correct active/pending parameter prefix.
Invalid persisted parameters throw before secret decryption, matchingStep, activation UPDATE or replay-counter CAS. Existing transaction finally/wrapper rollback paths remain intact.

Pending activation uses pending_created_at and no enabled/replay state. Active verification/find use original created_at, enabled_at and last_used_step. find retains its previous field mapping and model validation.
The existing model validates digest names case-insensitively while retaining the supplied string. Final helper preserves this behavior; no destructive normalization was added.
Expiry and valid-code control flow for valid persisted state is unchanged, including prior post-UPDATE/post-COMMIT time checks and factor/counter CAS predicates.
There are no new SQL queries, public signatures, schema migrations or cryptographic algorithms. A private value-construction/validation step is added to acceptance paths.

evidence_reviewed.original_probe: totp-persisted-parameters.json records original confirm=true, find=model exception, verify=true for three unsupported parameter sets.
evidence_reviewed.controls: 14 accepted controls cover periods 15/120, sha1/sha256/sha512 including uppercase/mixed-case spelling, 7/8 digits, later proof acceptance and single-use rejection.

evidence_boundary: Read-only independent source/test/log/XML review; no new execution or broad test gate was performed by this reviewer.
The demonstrated defect concerns persisted/imported metadata. Ordinary HTTP enrollment writes defaults and does not itself expose arbitrary period/digest selection.
The 15..120 period and digest allowlist are existing Componenta model rules, not claimed as universal RFC parameter restrictions.
Rejecting invalid persisted state is intended behavior correction. Malformed storage can now fail earlier, consistently with find(), instead of being used for authentication.
